chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who struck another man on his head with a tent-pole in a single blow, causing a penetrating wound until the blow reached the brain and his intellect departed. He عليه السلام said:

If the one struck does not comprehend from it the times of salat, and does not comprehend what he said nor what was said to him, then one waits with him for a year. If he dies within that period of a year, retaliation is carried out against his striker for him. But if he does not die within that year and his intellect does not return to him, his striker must pay the diyah from his own property for the loss of his intellect.

I said: Then what do you hold regarding the head-wound—anything upon him for it? He عليه السلام said: No, because he only struck him one blow, and that blow produced two injuries, so I imposed upon him the more severe of the two injuries, which is the diyah. But if he had struck him two blows, and the two blows produced two injuries, I would impose upon him the liability for what the two produced, whatever it may be, unless death were among them, in which case retaliation would be carried out against his striker for one, and the other would be set aside.

He عليه السلام said: And if he struck him three blows, one after another, and they produced three injuries, I would impose upon him the liability for what the three blows produced, whatever they may be, so long as death was not among them; otherwise retaliation would be carried out against his striker.

He said, and he عليه السلام said: And if he struck him ten blows and they produced one single injury, I would impose upon him that injury which those ten blows produced, whatever it may be, so long as death was not among it.

key_terms.أَوْقَاتَ الصَّلَاةِ: the times of salat used here as a sign of mental awareness
key_terms.أُقِيدَ بِهِ: retaliation is carried out against him
key_terms.الشَّجَّةِ: a head-wound or wound to the head
key_terms.جِنَايَتَيْنِ: two injuries or offenses resulting from an act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person is struck on the head and loses his intellect in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning bodily injury, loss of intellect, diyah, and retaliation. It explains that when a single blow causes multiple consequences, the more severe liability may apply, while multiple distinct blows can entail liability for each resulting injury unless death occurs, in which case qisas applies.
